incidents.vector: A Dutch-speaking caller posed as an Odido IT employee to trick customer-service staff into granting access to a customer contact system.
incidents.impact: Personal data of more than 6 million customers was stolen in the February breach; Dutch police now suspect a local accomplice and have seized servers used to distribute the data.

incidents.vector: Ransomware-as-a-service operation (The Gentlemen) using edge-device exploits, brute force, stolen credentials, a custom Go backdoor and an EDR-killer framework.
incidents.impact: The group has claimed roughly 580 victims across 77 countries since inception, becoming the second most active RaaS of 2026; manufacturing is the most targeted sector (103 victims).

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in a system that had not been updated for two years and dwelled in the network for over a week before detection.
incidents.impact: Ransomware disrupted mapping, hunting and contractor systems; ~44GB of internal data including credentials, certificates and source code was leaked. Two-thirds of contract customers still lacked access weeks later. Latvia's election infrastructure was confirmed unaffected.

incidents.vector: Large-scale automated scanning exploiting known vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins, Craft CMS, Joomla and other CMS software to deploy webshells for unauthenticated file upload, RCE, SSRF and deserialization.
incidents.impact: ACSC issued a critical alert; many small and medium Australian businesses were compromised, with webshells enabling defacement, credential capture, malware hosting and pivot into broader networks.

incidents.vector: Rebranded RaaS operation (Hyadina / 'GodDamn') used a Microsoft-signed malicious kernel driver (PoisonX) via BYOVD to kill security software, plus legitimate RMM tools and 14 open-source credential stealers.
incidents.impact: Symantec observed the group entrench in a victim environment and deploy its 'GodDamn' locker after disabling endpoint protection; the abuse of a Microsoft Hardware Compatibility-signed driver undermines standard defenses.

incidents.vector: A lone attacker used AI-assisted workflows to gain an AWS access key via an internet-facing app, then chained weaknesses across app services, CI/CD pipelines, source repos and data stores.
incidents.impact: Per Sygnia, the actor compromised a large AWS environment in ~72 hours, harvested secrets and credentials, created backdoors and demonstrated reversible disruption (blocking S3, zeroing ECS capacity) to extort the victim.

incidents.vector: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in third-party software used by an email platform KDDI operates for five Japanese internet service providers.
incidents.impact: More than 12.2 million customer email addresses and 7.6 million passwords were exposed; KDDI patched the flaw and mandated password resets, and said its own consumer email services were unaffected.

incidents.vector: A China-aligned cluster (tracked as UNK_MassTraction) chained two Roundcube webmail vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-42009, CVE-2025-49113); the initial exploit triggers on opening an email.
incidents.impact: Per Proofpoint, attackers targeted physics/engineering departments and researchers with national-security links to steal credentials and establish persistent access via webshells; fewer than 10 victims confirmed but dozens likely affected. Campaign assessed ongoing.

incidents.vector: China-nexus actor UAT-7810 exploits known n-day flaws in unpatched Ruckus and ASUS routers to deploy new custom backdoors (LONGLEASH, DOGLEASH, JARLEASH) and build Operational Relay Box networks.
incidents.impact: Per Cisco Talos, the group builds covert, resilient proxy infrastructure that secondary China-nexus APTs use to mask origins and attack high-value targets, creating a significant detection blind spot.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to certain corporate IT systems, reportedly linked to the ShinyHunters extortion group.
incidents.impact: The world's largest medical device company is notifying more than 3.8 million people that Social Security numbers, health data, names, contact details and dates of birth may have been exposed; 24 months of credit and identity monitoring offered.

incidents.vector: An AI agent (tracked as JadePuffer) exploited a Langflow RCE flaw (CVE-2025-3248), then pivoted to a production MySQL/Nacos server, running 600+ payloads and adapting to errors in seconds.
incidents.impact: Sysdig documented the first end-to-end LLM-driven extortion operation — reconnaissance through data theft, database deletion and ransom note — though a human still provisioned infrastructure and stolen credentials. Marks a lowered skill floor for ransomware.

incidents.victim: Klue customers (~20 firms incl. Recorded Future, Snyk, Tanium)
incidents.vector: Attackers breached Klue's network, stole OAuth tokens from customer accounts and used them to access connected Salesforce integrations.
incidents.impact: The victim list has grown to nearly 20 companies (including Huntress, Jamf, Deel, BeyondTrust, 8x8 and Blackbaud), with sensitive data stolen via the compromised third-party integration.

incidents.vector: One of Taiwan's largest mobile operators was hit by a newly launched ransomware operation (Settra).
incidents.impact: Pi Mobile says its mobile payments platform was not affected; Taiwan's Ministry of Digital Affairs opened an investigation into whether personal data was stolen.

incidents.vector: The Silent Ransom Group breached the American law firm in May 2026.
incidents.impact: The firm was breached and refused to pay a ransom; extent of stolen data not disclosed.

incidents.victim: Consumer IoT devices (smart TVs, streaming boxes)
incidents.vector: The NetNut / Popa residential-proxy botnet enrolled at least 2 million home devices via malicious SDKs bundled into apps and pre-installed on no-name streaming boxes.
incidents.impact: The FBI, IRS-CI, Google, Lumen and Shadowserver seized hundreds of domains, degrading the botnet by millions of devices. Google observed 316 threat clusters (criminal and espionage) using NetNut exit nodes to mask malicious traffic.

incidents.vector: Extortion group ShinyHunters (UNC6240) exploited a zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft (with a newer Oracle E-Business Suite flaw, CVE-2026-46817, now also seeing exploitation).
incidents.impact: Mandiant/Google assess 100+ organizations infiltrated, mostly higher education; confirmed victims include Nissan North America and medical supplier AdaptHealth. Data-theft extortion campaign is ongoing.

incidents.vector: Phishing-as-a-service platform 'ARToken' (linked to EvilTokens) abused Microsoft's OAuth device-code flow via vendor-impersonation invoice lures pointing to look-alike SharePoint tenants, bypassing MFA and capturing Primary Refresh Tokens.
incidents.impact: Talos recovered targeted lures spoofing a legitimate contractor to reach accounts-payable staff; the panel exposes 80+ endpoints for token persistence, inbox access, BEC and SharePoint exfiltration.

incidents.vector: Intruders breached the Homeland Security Information Network, targeting HSIN servers and a connected SharePoint system.
incidents.impact: The DHS network used to share sensitive data with federal, state, local and industry partners was compromised between late May and early June; the intruders and data taken remain unknown.

incidents.vector: The U.S. insurance sector's standards body was hacked at the start of June by the ShinyHunters group.
incidents.impact: NAIC suspended risk designations for insurers and some credit rating agencies paused data sharing to avoid exposure; NAIC says it has evicted the hackers and is restoring operations.

incidents.vector: Attackers stole customer data from the Japanese branch of the life-insurance company.
incidents.impact: More than 4.38 million customers were impacted; the Japan unit had also disclosed a breach the prior year.

incidents.vector: The World Leaks data-extortion group breached the Apple supplier and leaked stolen documents after the company refused to pay.
incidents.impact: Around 200,000 documents were leaked, including images of the upcoming iPhone 18's battery, chips and circuit boards, exposing supply-chain and product design data.

incidents.victim: North American academic, medical & research community
incidents.vector: PRC-nexus actor UNC6508 ran a sophisticated cross-sector campaign that remained undetected for over a year.
incidents.impact: Per Google Threat Intelligence Group, the actor targeted North American academic, medical and military research organizations, stealing data across academia, medicine, military, cybersecurity and foreign policy.

incidents.vector: Files allegedly taken from the central bank's network were leaked on the dark web by the Qilin ransomware group; officials traced the breach to an incident roughly three weeks earlier.
incidents.impact: Libyan authorities are investigating the breach of the country's central bank after leaked files appeared online.

incidents.vector: A new ransomware group ('BLackField') attacked the major Japanese components manufacturer.
incidents.impact: Nidec was forced to take its entire IT network offline and faces a $2 million ransom demand; the company was also hit by ransomware in late 2024.

incidents.vector: The Cyber Anarchy Squad, a Ukrainian hacktivist group, breached one of Russia's largest construction companies in May.
incidents.impact: The hackers claim to have wiped 3,000 servers and workstations and 700 virtual machines, deleted all backups, and stolen more than 650TB of sensitive documents.

incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — data theft / ad fraud
incidents.vector: A long-running operation ('StegoAd', active since ~2021) published 119 malicious Microsoft Edge extensions across 90+ developer accounts, using steganography to hide malicious code and delivering payloads days after install.
incidents.impact: Microsoft removed the extensions, which sought to steal credentials, backdoor browsers and commit ad / search-affiliate fraud; more than 2.6 million users are believed to have downloaded them, with Chrome and Firefox variants also involved.
